summary: Lake Erie light of 1848 at the west end of West Sister Island; keepers from 1847; automated 1937; island a wildlife refuge, closed to visitors.

lens.note: Fourth-order Fresnel installed 1857 (LighthouseFriends). Ten lamps and reflectors in 1848. The USLHS record gives a fourth-order original optic and a 300 mm optic as current.

structures.note: Forty feet, tapering from fifteen feet at the base to seven at the lantern (LighthouseFriends). USLHS record: 50.5 ft, limestone and brick. Interior brick cylinder added 1868 (LighthouseFriends).

Brick keeper's dwelling 20 by 30 ft near the tower (LighthouseFriends). The Board asked in 1866 for a new dwelling joined to the tower by a covered passage, built 1868 (LighthouseFriends). Second story added 1902. Abandoned in 1937.
Added in 1868 (LighthouseFriends). Moved about 250 feet (Light-House Board report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1896).
On a concrete foundation, lined with brick (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Not open to the public; visitors would threaten the nesting area (LighthouseFriends).

visit.note: Closed. Best seen from the water (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Coast Guard (lighthouse and five acres); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (refuge, 77 acres) (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Alexander A. Cromwell, first keeper on the roster (roster).
Conical stone tower built at the west end of the island; brick dwelling near the tower (LighthouseFriends).
Ten lamps backed by fourteen-inch reflectors (LighthouseFriends).
Fourth-order Fresnel lens installed in the tower's lantern (LighthouseFriends).
Light-House Board report: tower wall showed dampness, dwelling dilapidated; repairs requested (as quoted by LighthouseFriends).
Interior brick cylinder, cast-iron stairway, stone caps and sills, new lantern, and a new keeper's dwelling; appropriated 1867, work done 1868 (LighthouseFriends).
New boathouse added (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper Nathan Edson died at the station in February 1869 (LighthouseFriends; roster 1865-1869).
Well sunk through granite to 32 feet, replacing the cistern as the water supply (LighthouseFriends).
Pier built in 1887 destroyed by floating ice in February 1888 (LighthouseFriends).
Boat harbor built in 1889 soon damaged by floating ice (LighthouseFriends).
Circular iron oil house on a concrete foundation, lined with brick (LighthouseFriends).
Wharf extension corners fitted with wrought-iron plates against ice; boathouse moved some 250 feet (Light-House Board report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1896, item 1243).
New boatways built; protection crib work to shield the landing from the seas (Light-House Board report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1900, item 119).
Second story added to the keeper's dwelling (LighthouseFriends).

Keeper Chancie Fitzmorris rescued six persons from the yacht Luella, which capsized near the light in a squall, 7 September 1916 (Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1916, p. 39; LighthouseFriends gives five adults and a baby).
Keeper Fitzmorris, gored by a bull on 31 March 1919, was found after a red distress signal had burned about two weeks; a Marblehead lifesaving crew reached him (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper Fitzmorris rescued two men adrift in a disabled power boat for 36 hours, 10 May 1920 (Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1920, p. 28).
December 1927: keeper Gampher rescued two fishermen whose boat washed up on the island; an airplane sent to help crashed (LighthouseFriends).
Glazed part of the tower lantern removed, 3 July 1936; light shown from a lens lantern on top (LighthouseFriends).
West Sister Island Light automated; keeper's dwelling built in 1868 abandoned (LighthouseFriends).
President Roosevelt set the island aside as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds (LighthouseFriends).
Government designated 77 of the 82 acres as wilderness, January 1975 (LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives a fourth-order lens in 1848. LighthouseFriends says the 1848 light used ten lamps with reflectors and that a fourth-order Fresnel lens went in during 1857. The USLHS record also gives a fourth-order original optic from 1848, so the sources still disagree; the story follows LighthouseFriends.

corrections.proposed: stone (limestone and brick per USLHS; brick cylinder inside added 1868)
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends describes the tower as stone with an interior brick cylinder added in 1868; the USLHS record gives limestone and brick.
LighthouseFriends dates the fourth-order lens to 1857 and the 1848 light to ten lamps.

notes_for_editor: (1) Tower height: LighthouseFriends says forty feet (1848); the USLHS record says 50.5 ft; the record says 17.0 m (about 56 ft); Wikipedia's infobox says 55 ft (lead only, not cited). Not resolved; the story gives LighthouseFriends's figure and the USLHS figure. (2) Lens: the USLHS record gives 'FOURTH ORDER' as original and '300 MM' as current; LighthouseFriends says ten lamps in 1848 and a fourth-order lens in 1857. (3) Dwellings: LighthouseFriends describes a brick dwelling near the tower in 1848, and a new dwelling built in 1868 after the Board's 1866 request. It does not say whether the 1848 house was replaced. (4) Corpus items: the 1896 item is in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1896 (title page read; scan p. 159 confirmed by the page index). The 1900 item is in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1900 (title page read); its scan p. 184 is not confirmed, because that volume has no page index. Printed pages are not confirmed. The Bulletin pages are PDF pages. (5) Newspapers: Chronicling America search 'Fitzmorris' with 'West Sister', 1916-1920, found no hits. The 1869 deaths, the 1919 goring and the 1927 rescue rest on LighthouseFriends alone; its own sources (Toledo Blade 1929; Detroit Free Press 2003) were not read. (6) The 1916 count: the Bulletin says six persons; LighthouseFriends says five adults and a baby (six people), which agree. (7) Harriet B. Haynes's relationship to Harrison Haynes is not stated in the sources read. (8) The WWII artillery practice has no year in the sources read, so it is not in the events list. (9) Wikipedia (not cited) gives 1937 automation and a refuge established 1937; both agree with LighthouseFriends. (10) The 1916 capsizing place disagrees: the Bulletin says near the light station in a squall; LighthouseFriends says two miles west of the island. The story states both. (11) The lens disagreement is stated in the text: LighthouseFriends dates the fourth-order lens to 1857; the USLHS record gives a fourth-order original optic installed in 1848. (12) The story's 1916 and 1920 rescues cite the Bulletin pages (PDF pages 39 and 28, both confirmed by the page index).
